solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Also chasing university place in Pennines? (6)

indicatorNotes.chasing: to chase is to run along behind, so this piece comes after the ones it follows

blocks.note: U = university
Pl. = place, as in street names
and = also

annotation.surface: A student taking up a university place up in the Pennines.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Place in Pennines' looks like the definition, but 'place' is needed for PL; the definition is just 'in Pennines?'. The Pennines are the hill range down northern England, and the question mark flags an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Upland describes high country, and anything in the Pennines, England's central hill chain, is exactly that: a definition by example.

entries.clue: Offence taken: Greek character quite expressing it (5)

indicatorNotes.expressing: to express is, in its old sense, to press out, as juice from fruit, so these letters are squeezed out of the word

blocks.note: pi, a letter of the Greek alphabet
QUITE with IT pressed out

annotation.surface: Someone takes offence at a Greek who speaks their mind rather bluntly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Expressing' reads as saying something; here it is the older sense of squeezing out, as with juice.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fit of pique is resentment at a slight, the feeling of having taken offence.

entries.clue: Duck, upon removing tail, is around right weight (11)

indicatorNotes.removing tail: a word's tail is its last letter, and removing it cuts that letter off
indicatorNotes.around: around means surrounding, so the first word wraps itself about the letter

blocks.note: to duck a question is to avoid it; this word goes round the R
R = right
UPON without its last letter N
used as printed

annotation.surface: A cook trims a duck's tail and weighs the bird.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the bird in the surface but the verb in the wordplay. Avoirdupois is the pounds-and-ounces system of weight still used in Britain and America.
annotation.definitionFit: Avoirdupois is the system of pounds and ounces, and by extension weight itself, often jokingly of a person's bulk.

entries.clue: Groom on time as horse moves? (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, one thing on another sits above it, so the first piece is written first

blocks.note: to groom is to dress, as hair or a horse's coat
an age = a time, an era

annotation.surface: A stable hand grooms a horse in time for it to be moved on.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Groom' looks like the stable job; it gives DRESS. The question mark marks a loose definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competitive discipline of trained horse movements, so the definition describes it rather than naming it.

entries.clue: Hurried to gobble crackers before a fasting period (7)

indicatorNotes.to gobble: to gobble is to swallow greedily, so the first word takes the next ones inside it
indicatorNotes.before: before means ahead of, so the word it follows comes first

blocks.note: ran = hurried; it holds the rest
crackers = mad, crazy
used as printed; it follows MAD inside the outer word

annotation.surface: Someone rushes to wolf down biscuits before a fast begins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crackers' is the biscuit in the surface and the adjective in the wordplay. The 'a' does double duty, as a letter and as the start of the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of fasting from dawn to dusk, so the definition describes it by kind.

entries.clue: Studies concerned with first note from the sign (5)

blocks.note: re = concerning, as in memo headings
A is the first note of the scale A to G
D.S., dal segno, the musical instruction to repeat from the sign

annotation.surface: A musician studies the score from the first note to the repeat sign.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's musical words hide two of the pieces: 'first note' is A, and 'from the sign' is the Italian dal segno, abbreviated D.S. on a score.
annotation.definitionFit: A British sense: to read a subject is to study it at university, as in reading law.

entries.clue: Spooner’s tide guide that reduces deposits on estate? (7)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Rev. William Spooner was famous for swapping the first sounds of two words, so his version of a phrase does the same

blocks.note: a flood map charts where the tide will reach; swap its opening sounds FL and M

annotation.surface: A chart of the tides, as mangled by Reverend Spooner.
annotation.walkthrough: FLOOD MAP swaps to MUD FLAP. 'Estate' is an estate car, the British name for a station wagon, not land; the flap stops dirt being thrown up onto it.
annotation.definitionFit: A mudflap hangs behind a wheel and cuts down the mud sprayed onto the car, the deposits on the estate.

entries.clue: Dispirited? Practical lesson one’s put into action (11)

indicatorNotes.put into: things put into something are placed inside it, so these pieces go inside the word for action

blocks.note: a deed = an action; it takes the rest inside
the moral of a story is its practical lesson
one = I, plus the 's; this follows MORAL

annotation.surface: A teacher wonders whether a hands-on lesson will lift a gloomy pupil.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Practical lesson' looks like a class; it is the moral of a fable. The question mark only turns the surface into a question.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who has lost heart and confidence is dispirited.

entries.clue: Present time, or at some time after noon (5)

indicatorNotes.after: after means following, so this piece is written behind the letter it follows

blocks.note: n. = noon, a dictionary abbreviation
once = at some time, formerly

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether now suits, or sometime in the afternoon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After noon' reads as afternoon; split, it puts ONCE after N.
annotation.definitionFit: An old word surviving in an idiom: 'for the nonce' means for the present occasion.

entries.clue: Mushroom where batter needs to stand? (8)

blocks.note: to mushroom is to grow fast
a cricket batsman stands in the crease, the line marked in front of the stumps

annotation.surface: A cook wonders where the batter should rest before the mushrooms go in.
annotation.walkthrough: Batter looks like pancake mix; it is the cricket batsman, who is safe from being run out while in the crease. Read as two words, IN CREASE, that is where he stands.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb sense: to mushroom is to grow suddenly and fast, like mushrooms overnight.

entries.clue: Some guts needed to help win Test in England (9)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the answer is found inside the words that follow

blocks.note: starts after the W and ends at the E of England

annotation.surface: It will take some courage to win a Test match in England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Guts' is courage in the surface and the literal bowels in the definition. A Test is a Test match, cricket's five-day international game.
annotation.definitionFit: Guts are the bowels, and this is one part of them, hence 'some guts'.

entries.clue: Key locks office (5)

blocks.note: C is a musical key
locks = hair

annotation.surface: A key that locks an office door.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Key' and 'locks' pair up as door hardware; one is the key of C and the other is hair.
annotation.definitionFit: An office in the sense of a post: a professorship or the headship of a committee is a chair.

entries.clue: Doctor Evadne rued nothing — made determined effort (11)

indicatorNotes.Doctor: to doctor is to tamper with or falsify, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder
nothing = O, zero

annotation.surface: Evadne regrets doing nothing, despite having tried hard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' sits first like a title before Evadne's name; it is the verb, to tamper with.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to endeavour is to strive, to make a determined effort.

entries.clue: Problem with battle order (7)

blocks.note: a sum = an arithmetic problem
the Battle of Mons, 1914, in Belgium

annotation.surface: A general has trouble with the order of battle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Order of battle' is a military phrase that splits here: 'battle' is Mons and 'order' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a command to appear, as before a court, is an order.

entries.clue: Flying squadron tutored madmen that needed proving (4,4,13)

indicatorNotes.Flying: flying things are scattered and in motion, so the letters fly about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 21 letters

annotation.surface: A squadron of airmen trained a band of lunatics, and the result had to be proved.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flying squadron' reads as an air force unit; 'Flying' is the instruction and the squadron is only letters. The Latin phrase closes a proof, abbreviated QED.
annotation.definitionFit: The Latin means 'which was to be demonstrated', written at the end of a proof: that is, the thing that needed proving.

entries.clue: Money in undefined amount MI6’s obsession? (8)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the money goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: n is the mathematician's unspecified number
MI6 is the Secret Intelligence Service, SIS, Britain's foreign spy agency
the euro, a currency; it goes between the other two pieces

annotation.surface: A spy agency's fixation with an unknown sum of money.
annotation.walkthrough: The money sits between the unknown amount and the spy agency. The question mark marks the definition as loose: an obsession is one kind of neurosis.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an obsession is a kind of neurosis, the anxious mental disorder.

entries.clue: SLR shot captures wingless bird and those lingering (7)

indicatorNotes.shot: something shot is wrecked, so these three letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.captures: to capture is to take and hold, so the rearranged letters hold the bird inside
indicatorNotes.wingless: a word's wings are its outer letters, so both ends are clipped off

blocks.note: anagram fodder; an SLR is a single-lens reflex camera
TURKEY without its outer letters T and Y

annotation.surface: A photographer's camera snaps a flightless bird and the people hanging about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'captures' look like photography, but one scrambles SLR and the other puts the clipped bird inside. The bird is a turkey.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who lurk hang about out of sight, lingering.

entries.clue: This was capital offence — leader denied motive (6)

indicatorNotes.leader denied: the leader of a word is its first letter, and denying it takes that letter away

blocks.note: treason was punished by death, a capital offence
drop the first letter T

annotation.surface: An old hanging crime whose ringleader refused to give a motive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city; it means punishable by death, as treason was in Britain until 1998.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the reason for an act is its motive.

entries.clue: Circle of PC gurus may form research panel (5,5)

indicatorNotes.may form: to form is to shape, so the letters are shaped into a new word

blocks.note: a circle is shaped like O
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A ring of computer experts could make up a research panel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Circle' seems to be a group of people, which suits the answer; it is just the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A focus group is a small panel of people whose views are gathered for market or political research.

entries.clue: Theodoric, perhaps ridiculously short, having to go back inside (9)

indicatorNotes.ridiculously: something done ridiculously is done absurdly, so the letters are thrown into an absurd order
indicatorNotes.having: to have is to hold, so the rearranged word holds the next piece
indicatorNotes.back: back means backwards, so the letters run in reverse
indicatorNotes.inside: inside means within, so the reversed piece sits within the other

blocks.note: anagram fodder; it wraps the next piece
used as printed, then run backwards

annotation.surface: A historian mocks the stature of a Gothic king.
annotation.walkthrough: Theodoric the Great ruled the Ostrogoths, the eastern Goths who took Italy in the 490s. SHORT is scrambled around the backwards TO GO.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Theodoric the Great was the most famous Ostrogoth, king of Italy around AD 500.

entries.clue: Snakes concealed in ideal state as Roman leaves (7)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed within, so the word for concealed goes inside the other
indicatorNotes.leaves: to leave is to go away, so these letters drop out

blocks.note: Thomas More's imaginary perfect commonwealth
ut is Latin for 'as'; these letters leave the front
hid = concealed; it goes inside what remains

annotation.surface: Snakes lurking in paradise once the Romans have gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As Roman' means the Latin for 'as', which is UT; taking it from UTOPIA leaves OPIA to hold HID. The surface nods to the serpent in Eden.
annotation.definitionFit: Ophidia is the zoologists' name for the snakes as a group, from the Greek for serpent.

entries.clue: Liquid gold is enough for private home (7,5)

indicatorNotes.Liquid: a liquid flows and takes any shape, so the letters run into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: Ready money will buy you a private home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Liquid gold' reads as cash in hand, or as molten metal; 'Liquid' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A lodging house is a private house where rooms are let to lodgers, a home for them.

entries.clue: Indecisive People’s Princess meeting the syndicate (9)

blocks.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, called 'the People's Princess' by Tony Blair on her death
used as printed
a ring = a syndicate, as of dealers or smugglers

annotation.surface: Diana can't make up her mind about meeting a business consortium.
annotation.walkthrough: 'People's Princess' is the phrase Tony Blair used for Diana in 1997, so it gives DI.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone dithering keeps wavering and cannot decide.

entries.clue: Spirit died, endlessly blessed in churchyard (4,4)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: without an end, so the word loses its last letter

blocks.note: go = spirit, energy, as in 'full of go'
d. = died, as in family trees
sacred = blessed; lose the last letter

annotation.surface: A spirit, once dead, lies blessed in the churchyard.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' wants to be a ghost, the one surface a churchyard invites; it is GO, vigour.
annotation.definitionFit: God's acre is an old, rather poetic term for a churchyard used for burial.

entries.clue: German foundation leaving bishop millions (4)

indicatorNotes.leaving: things leaving a word go out of it, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: the bottom of something is its foundation
B = bishop, in chess notation; it leaves the front
M = millions; it leaves the end

annotation.surface: A German fund pulls a bishop's millions out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foundation' looks like a charity with money to give, but it is BOTTOM.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Otto is a typical German man's name, borne by Bismarck and several emperors.

entries.clue: Solidly-built pupils lacking in academic promise? (5-3)

blocks.note: stocky, heavily built
a set is a class grouped by ability, and thick means dim

annotation.surface: A school's bottom stream, burly and not very bright.
annotation.walkthrough: British schools split year groups into sets by ability, so the least able form a THICK SET.
annotation.definitionFit: Thickset means stocky and heavily built, the same sense as solidly built.

entries.clue: Church medic visiting animal to restore to good condition (9)

indicatorNotes.visiting: a visitor goes into someone's place, so the medic goes inside the word

blocks.note: a cat is an animal; it comes first
to heal is to restore to health
Dr = doctor

annotation.surface: A church doctor calls on a sick animal to nurse it back to health.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Medic visiting' reads as a vet's house call; visiting means going inside, so the doctor sits in the word for restore.
annotation.definitionFit: A cathedral is a church, specifically the principal one of a diocese: a definition by broader class.

entries.clue: Gold found in crazily loaded place invading Spaniards sought (2,6)

indicatorNotes.found in: something found in a place is inside it, so this piece sits inside the rest
indicatorNotes.crazily: crazily means in a mad way, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
anagram fodder; it wraps the gold

annotation.surface: Conquistadors hunt for a city crammed with gold.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loaded' sits beside gold as wealth; it is only letters to shuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold that Spanish conquistadors searched for in South America.

entries.clue: Harsh one with no heart maybe brought up a name (9) avoiding repetition of (9)

indicatorNotes.brought up: in a down clue, something brought up is raised from bottom to top, so these letters read upwards

blocks.note: one = I, the Roman numeral
no used as printed, joined on by 'with'
a heart is one kind of playing card
used as printed
N = name
stray text left over from the source page, not part of this clue; ignore it

annotation.surface: A heartless person, perhaps, raised a name.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One with no heart' looks like a description of the harsh person; it is three pieces run upwards. Draco was an Athenian lawgiver whose laws were famously severe. The words after the first (9) are scraping debris.
annotation.definitionFit: Named after Draco of Athens, whose laws punished almost everything by death, so draconian means excessively harsh.

entries.clue: Penny possibly closing the show devours rook and turtle part (8)

indicatorNotes.devours: to devour is to swallow, so the rook ends up inside the phrase

blocks.note: p = penny
an act that closes the show goes on last; it swallows the rook
R = rook, in chess notation

annotation.surface: A performer called Penny, topping the bill, eats a rook and some turtle.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Penny' reads as a woman's name; it is P. The act closing the show is the one on last, and the rook goes inside that phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: The plastron is the flat underside of a turtle's or tortoise's shell.

entries.clue: Cheered about one touch from the right for United (12)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so the first word goes round the rest
indicatorNotes.from the right: read from the right means read backwards, as English runs left to right

blocks.note: to console is to cheer someone up; it goes round the rest
one = I
a tad = a touch, a small amount

annotation.surface: Fans cheered a late winner for Manchester United.
annotation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like the football club; it is the definition, as merged or combined.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: firms or forces merged into a single whole are united.

entries.clue: Artist returned with long face, related to structure close to the heart (10)

annotation.definition: related to structure close to the heart

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: an epic is long, on a grand scale
RA = Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
dial is slang for a face

annotation.surface: A painter comes home glum, dealing with something close to their heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Long face' reads as sulky; it splits into two separate pieces, with the backwards artist between them.
annotation.definitionFit: Epicardial describes the epicardium, the inner layer of the membrane wrapped round the heart.

entries.clue: Elemental form is uppermost in Phoebe’s heart (7)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed within, so the word for uppermost goes inside
indicatorNotes.heart: the heart of a word is its centre, so take its middle letters

blocks.note: used as printed
the two middle letters of PHOEBE
top = uppermost; it goes between those two letters

annotation.surface: Something elemental is foremost in Phoebe's heart.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heart' could mean feelings; it takes the middle of PHOEBE, which has six letters and so two at its centre.
annotation.definitionFit: Each isotope is a form of a chemical element with a different number of neutrons.

entries.clue: Short story involving short Scottish prosecutor: that’s appropriate (10)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is to wrap up in, so the story wraps round the prosecutor
indicatorNotes.short: a word cut short loses its last letter

blocks.note: a conte is a short story, from French
the procurator fiscal is Scotland's public prosecutor, called the fiscal for short; lose the last letter

annotation.surface: A brief tale about a Scottish lawyer, told because it suits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb, to seize. The second 'short' clips FISCAL.
annotation.definitionFit: To appropriate is to take something for your own use, as authorities confiscate goods.

entries.clue: A small horse gypsies reared under substantial illusion (4,7)

indicatorNotes.reared: something reared is raised upright, so in a down clue these letters read upwards
indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, below, so these letters are written after the one they sit under

blocks.note: fat = substantial, as a fat cheque; it sits on top
used as printed
a nag is a small or poor horse
the Roma, the Romani people

annotation.surface: A pony that travellers raised proves a grand mirage.
annotation.walkthrough: A, NAG and ROMA together run upwards, under FAT. The phrase is Italian for Morgan le Fay, whose sorcery was blamed for the mirages of the Strait of Messina.
annotation.definitionFit: A fata morgana is a complex mirage, often over the sea, so an optical illusion.

entries.clue: For whom getting back to work should be a professional priority? (12)

annotation.definition: For whom getting back to work should be a professional priority?

blocks.clueFragment: For whom getting back to work
blocks.note: the surface means returning to the job after time off; the setter means making a patient's back function
for this practitioner, backs are the entire profession

annotation.surface: Who most needs to return to the office?
annotation.walkthrough: The phrase 'getting back to work' sounds like the end of a holiday. Read literally, it is a spine being made to work again.
annotation.definitionFit: A chiropractor treats the spine by manipulation, so making backs work properly is the whole job.

entries.clue: Electra and Priscilla are so unsympathetic (4-7)

blocks.note: the middle letter of each name is C, and C = cold, as on a tap
lacking warmth or feeling

annotation.surface: Two women are said to be heartless.
annotation.walkthrough: Electra has seven letters and Priscilla nine, and both have C at their centre: C is cold on a tap, so each is C-hearted.
annotation.definitionFit: Unsympathetic people lack warmth, so they are cold at heart, and the names literally have cold hearts.

entries.clue: Two things hair stylist did as arranged (3,3,5)

blocks.note: a stylist cuts hair, then dries it
settled beforehand, fixed

annotation.surface: A hairdresser does two jobs, as booked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' suggests the hair itself being styled; it is the idiom for something already decided.
annotation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something settled in advance and not open to change: already arranged.

entries.clue: Articles drawn from Cairo and Tehran reversed artificial expression (8)

indicatorNotes.drawn from: things drawn from a word are pulled out of it, so the articles go
indicatorNotes.reversed: something reversed runs the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: A and AN, the indefinite articles, are to be removed
CAIRO without A
TEHRAN without AN

annotation.surface: Grand speeches from two Middle Eastern capitals, turned around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Articles' suggests newspaper pieces; it means the grammatical articles A and AN.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhetoric in its disparaging sense is showy, insincere language: artificial expression.

entries.clue: Section‘s second district in French city (9)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so these letters go within the city

blocks.note: Caen, in Normandy; it holds the rest
s = second
an area = a district

annotation.surface: A section of a French city is its second district.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Section' looks like a part of a town; it is a caesarean section, the surgical birth.
annotation.definitionFit: A caesarean section is the operation of delivering a baby through the abdomen, usually shortened to 'section' or 'caesarean'.

entries.clue: Letters central to belief in tract showing faith (8)

indicatorNotes.central to: letters central to a word are its middle ones
indicatorNotes.in: in means placed within, so those letters go inside the tract

blocks.note: a tract of land is a region; it holds the other letters
the middle two letters of BELIEF

annotation.surface: A religious tract shows the reader what lies at the heart of belief.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tract' in a faith setting is a pamphlet; here it is a stretch of land.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a religion is a faith, such as Islam or Christianity.

entries.clue: Weak husband opening airtight container (4)

indicatorNotes.opening: a tin opener gets inside a tin, so the husband goes inside the container

blocks.note: a tin is a sealed can
h = husband

annotation.surface: A feeble man struggles to open a tin.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Weak husband' reads as a description of him; the definition is only 'Weak'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: thin tea or a thin excuse is weak.

entries.clue: Maiden in a high-pitched voice, quavering lyrically (8)

indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the maiden goes inside the voice

blocks.note: used as printed
a treble is a high singing voice, a boy's soprano
M = maiden, a maiden over in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A girl sings in a shrill voice, trembling as she goes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' is the girl in the surface; it is cricket's maiden over, M on a scorecard. 'Lyrically' flags a poetic word.
annotation.definitionFit: Atremble is a poetic word for trembling, which is what quavering means; 'lyrically' marks the register.

entries.clue: Former empire’s vulgar riches? (12)

blocks.note: the association of nations that grew out of the British Empire
common = vulgar, wealth = riches

annotation.surface: A former empire flaunts its tasteless wealth.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is read as two words, COMMON WEALTH; the question mark marks that playful split.
annotation.definitionFit: The Commonwealth is the club of nations, mostly once British colonies, that succeeded the empire: the former empire in its present form.

entries.clue: Old Tuareg sullied in scandal (7)

indicatorNotes.sullied: something sullied is spoiled, so the letters are disturbed from their order

blocks.note: O = old
anagram fodder; the Tuareg are nomads of the Sahara

annotation.surface: An elderly Saharan nomad is disgraced in a scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: The Tuareg are a Berber people of the Sahara; the name is used only for its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking act that causes public anger, so a scandal.

entries.clue: Go to bed with upper-class lodger — army officer (10)

blocks.note: to lie down, as in bed
U = upper-class, as opposed to non-U
a tenant rents a room or house

annotation.surface: Sleeping with the posh lodger turns out to mean sleeping with a soldier.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go to bed with' sounds like an affair; it gives LIE, and 'with' joins it to the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by rank: this is a junior commissioned officer's title in the British Army.

entries.clue: Large insect regularly nearing light (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so take every other letter

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing
an ant is an insect
the second, fourth and sixth letters of NEARING

annotation.surface: A big moth flutters closer and closer to the light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large insect' reads as one thing, a moth heading for the flame; it splits into L and ANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable light in a protective case.

entries.clue: Initially sober, then learning about solid alcohol (6)

indicatorNotes.Initially: initially means at the start, so take the first letter of each word
indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned round, so these letters are read backwards

blocks.note: first letters of SOBER and THEN
lore = learning, knowledge

annotation.surface: Sober at first, then reading up about hard spirits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solid alcohol' sounds like a joke about strong drink; in chemistry, alcohols are a class of compounds, and some are solids.
annotation.definitionFit: A sterol, such as cholesterol, is a steroid alcohol, solid at room temperature.

entries.clue: Philosopher‘s topless fellow outside clubs (5)

indicatorNotes.topless: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so it is cut off
indicatorNotes.outside: outside means surrounding, so the man goes round the clubs

blocks.note: BLOKE, a fellow, without its first letter
C = clubs, the card suit

annotation.surface: A philosopher is a shirtless bloke standing outside nightclubs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topless' is racy in the surface; it just drops the top letter of BLOKE. John Locke was the 17th-century English philosopher.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: John Locke, the English empiricist, is one philosopher.

entries.clue: Sat after collapse in a wine store, choose not to drink (7)

indicatorNotes.after collapse: after it has collapsed, the word is in a heap, so its letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.in: in means inside, so the rearranged letters go into the rest

blocks.note: anagram fodder
used as printed
a bin is a rack or cellar for wine bottles; it holds the rearranged letters

annotation.surface: After collapsing in the wine cellar, someone decides to stay off the drink.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wine store' suggests a shop; a wine bin is the rack in a cellar. The surface is a hangover story.
annotation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain, especially from alcohol, so choosing not to drink.

entries.clue: One among parrots ascending displays reddish-brown shade (5)

indicatorNotes.among: among means amid, so one goes in with the other letters
indicatorNotes.ascending: in a down clue, ascending means going up, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: one = I
to parrot or ape is to imitate; the I goes after its first letter

annotation.surface: A flock of parrots rising shows a brownish colour.
